svg.title: A toolbox release arrives — copier update preserves my work — a toolbox update splits the dictionary, keeps my word, and spares my edits
svg.text: A toolbox release arrives — copier update preserves my
Scenario: a toolbox update splits the dictionary, keeps my word, and spares my edits
The update splits the dictionary and keeps my word
A flipped answer delivers new tools and spares my edits

g.text: Given a developer's project was generated from an earlier toolbox
release
A project made with an older toolbox (release 22.0.0), from before the spelling dictionary
was split. The line on screen shows which toolbox version it came from.
And its spelling dictionary is a single framework-owned file
At this old release the whole spelling dictionary is one file, config.json — the only place
a project can add its own words.
And the developer has added their own word inside that shared file
The developer's own word (Caddyfile) sits inside config.json, mixed in with the framework's
own words.
When the developer runs the toolbox update in the terminal
The exact command Renovate runs on its own to move to release 22.7.1. It refreshes the
dictionary and moves the developer's word to its own file.
Then the project now tracks the new toolbox release
The project is now on release 22.7.1 — the version line has moved forward.
And its dictionary has been split into three files
The one dictionary is now three files: config.json, config.base.json (framework words) and
config.project.json (project words).
And the framework keeps its own words in its own file
The framework's own words now live in config.base.json — the developer's word is not among
them.
And the developer's own word has moved to a project-owned file
The developer's word (Caddyfile) has moved to config.project.json, the file a toolbox update
never overwrites.
And the shared file itself is now empty — it only imports the other two
config.json now holds no words of its own; it only pulls in the other two files.
Given a project generated from an earlier toolbox release carries the
developer's own edit
Off-camera: a versioned template (releases 1.0.0 → 1.0.1), a project generated at 1.0.0,
then the developer appends their own marker to project/Taskfile.yml — a copier
skip-if-exists file an update must never overwrite.
And the project has no Ansible configuration yet
With the default answers the generated project has no Ansible tooling: grepping .config for
ansible finds nothing.
When the developer re-runs the toolbox update and turns the Ansible
option on
The same `copier update`, this time answering ansible_enabled=true: the same grep now finds
the ansible and ansible-lint entries the flip delivered.
Then the new Ansible tooling is delivered by the update
The flipped answer delivers the release's Ansible tooling — .config/ansible and
.config/ansible-lint.
And the developer's own edit survived the update untouched
project/Taskfile.yml still carries the developer's marker after the update — the
skip-if-exists file was never overwritten.
